data.heading: Where it started
data.description: Orders stuck in problem states and thousands of tickets a month, all resolved by hand.

blocks.title: Business problem
blocks.body: Between 3% and 10% of orders ran into problems and needed manual fixing. 2,500 to 3,000 tickets arrived every month, and every incident was resolved manually.

blocks.title: Technical barriers
blocks.body: Every monitoring tool had to feed its data in, with thresholds set carefully enough to avoid false-positive alerts across 200+ microservices and applications.

blocks.title: Agivant's role
blocks.body: AIOps architecture, ML and NLP model development, integration across 200+ microservices, and automated recovery

data.heading: What Agivant built
data.description: Agivant built the framework on a BigPanda-based architecture for monitoring, event correlation, de-duplication, enrichment, and escalation, and integrated 200+ microservices and applications. Models train on data gathered from every relevant source and retrain regularly. In production, each incoming incident or alert runs through the models, which predict its category and its solution and publish both to a dashboard where the support team acts. Value in days and weeks.

blocks.title: BigPanda event pipeline
blocks.body: Monitoring, event correlation, de-duplication, enrichment, and escalation for 200+ integrated microservices and applications.

blocks.title: Anomaly detection
blocks.body: AIOps identifies anomalies across the integrated estate.

blocks.title: Problem categorization
blocks.body: AI, ML, and NLP models classify each incoming incident.

blocks.title: Solution prediction
blocks.body: Models predict the likely solution for each incident and suggest the recovery action.

blocks.title: Single-click recovery
blocks.body: The support team triggers the suggested recovery from the dashboard with one click.

blocks.title: Auto-recovery for known patterns
blocks.body: Known failure patterns recover automatically, with no manual step.

blocks.title: Defects from application logs
blocks.body: Code and data issues found in application logs are raised as defects, and the code fixes that follow reduce incoming tickets.

blocks.title: Single-pane dashboard
blocks.body: Health information on systems, applications, and incidents in one view.

blocks.title: Train and retrain loop
blocks.body: Models train on data from all relevant sources and retrain regularly, with support team feedback feeding each cycle.

blocks.title: Before
blocks.body: Manual incident resolution, 2,500 to 3,000 tickets a month, and 3% to 10% of orders needing hand fixes.

blocks.title: After
blocks.body: Correlated events feeding ML predictions, auto-recovery for known patterns, defects raised from logs, and one health dashboard.

data.heading: Proof in production
data.description: Data from every relevant source trains the models, and they retrain regularly. When an incident or alert comes in, the models predict its category and its solution and publish both to the dashboard. Known patterns recover automatically, and the support team acts on the rest with a single click. Code and data issues found in application logs become defects, and the code fixes that follow brought incoming tickets from 2,500 to 3,000 a month down to 500 to 600, with average process time down from 30 minutes to 3.

blocks.heading: Measured results
blocks.description: Incident resolution moved from manual work to AIOps-driven handling, with 90% savings.

blocks.title: Reusable asset
blocks.body: The trained models and their retraining loop stay with the framework, so every new incident and every support team action feeds the next prediction. Every build amplifies the next.

blocks.title: Challenges overcome
blocks.body: The AIOps service needed receiver and feeder APIs into a cloud-based solution, and those APIs had to clear security review before integration could proceed.
